Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rsahelpers 0.2.0

This release brings the model family of the RSA package to the latent Mplus workflow: restricted response surface models, a runner and a comparison table for the family, a shared metric for the X and Y factors, and intervals for derived surface parameters. The defaults reproduce the output of 0.1.0.

Restricted response surface models

  • create_rsa_mplus_model() and rsa_mplus_workflow() gain rsa_model, which generates the restricted second-order models of RSA::RSA() as latent Mplus models: the fit-pattern models "SRRR", "SRR", "RR", "SRSQD", "SSQD", and "SQD", as well as "IA", "additive", "mean", "diff", "onlyx", "onlyy", "onlyx2", "onlyy2", and "null". Terms set to zero are fixed with @0; the other restrictions and the ridge parameters c, s, bm, and a4r (RSA’s C, S, meaneffect, and a4.rescaled) are written in MODEL CONSTRAINT. The rotated ridge models express b3 as a function of the other weights, so a single run fits ridges and troughs. Surface and principal-axis parameters that a model fixes or leaves undefined are not generated. start takes start values, for example from the fitted full model.

  • rsa_model also accepts four models that are not in the RSA package: "addx2" and "addy2" (the plane with one squared term), "noIA" (no product term), and "a5zero" (equal squared terms, which nests "SRR" and "IA").

  • RSA_mplus() gains rsa_model, which names the fitted model in the RSA package’s family ("additive", "IA", "SQD", "onlyx", "null", and so on). Terms the model sets to zero may be dropped from the Mplus syntax or left without a label, and are then returned as 0. They are listed in the new omitted_terms element. Terms the model estimates must still be found, and a nonzero estimate for a term the model sets to zero is an error. By default the model is taken from a generated workflow and is otherwise "full", as before. Surface parameters that the model fixes at zero are shown as 0 in the plot annotation.

Fitting and comparing the model family

  • New fit_rsa_mplus_family() writes, runs, and reads a set of latent RSA models from one specification, by default the 14 models that RSA::RSA() fits. The full model is fitted first and its estimates are the start values of the others. A model that fails is recorded with the stage at which it failed, and the other models are still fitted. The four additional models are fitted when they are named in models. Input files are named in lower case (rsa_srrr.inp), because Mplus lower-cases file names and would not find rsa_SRRR.inp on a case-sensitive file system.

  • New compare_rsa_mplus_models() compares the fitted models, modelled on RSA::aictab() and RSA::compare(). Models are ranked by AICc (counting all free parameters, including the measurement model) with Akaike weights and evidence ratios. Each restricted model is tested against the full model with the Satorra-Bentler scaled likelihood-ratio test from the MLR log-likelihoods and scaling correction factors; reference names another model to test against, and the models nested in it are then tested. The table also has the R-square of the latent outcome and flags failed or non-converged runs, Mplus errors and warnings, a model that fits better than a model it is nested in (with a warning), ridge lines of the SRRR, SRR, SRSQD, and SSQD models that lie far outside the data or rotated ridge models at b5 = 0, and a scaled test with cd <= 0.

A shared metric for X and Y

  • create_rsa_mplus_model(), rsa_mplus_workflow(), and fit_rsa_mplus_family() gain identification and center. identification = "effects" puts each factor on the metric of its average indicator (effects coding). center = "pooled" gives the X and Y factors one shared origin, so the latent line X = Y is equality on the response scale, as in RSA::RSA(center = "pooled"). It requires identification = "effects" or "invariance".

  • identification = "invariance" is a second way to put the X and Y factors on one metric. Matched X and Y indicators share their loadings and intercepts, the marker intercepts are fixed at 0, and both factor means are freed. Unlike effects coding, this writes no MODEL CONSTRAINT statements for the measurement model, so it runs under ESTIMATOR = BAYES, and it is a testable restriction. free_intercepts frees the intercepts of single indicator pairs (partial scalar invariance).

  • New fit_rsa_mplus_invariance() writes, runs, and compares configural, metric, partial scalar, and scalar invariance models of one or more X/Y factor pairs, with Satorra-Bentler scaled chi-square difference tests.

Intervals and the supported region

  • New rsa_mplus_draws() gives Monte Carlo intervals for the surface parameters of a model estimated by maximum likelihood. It draws b1 to b5 from their asymptotic distribution (TECH3), imposes the restrictions of rsa_model, and computes a1 to a5 and the ridge or principal-axis parameters on each draw.

  • New rsa_mplus_supported_range() gives the range of the lines of congruence and incongruence that the data support, from the model-implied distribution of the latent X and Y factors.

Minor improvements and fixes

  • Mplus is now found from WSL when only the Windows executable (Mplus.exe) is on the PATH.

  • run_rsa_mplus_model() explains the failure when Mplus wrote a lower-cased output file next to an input file whose name has capital letters, which happens on case-sensitive file systems (Linux, WSL). Give modelout a lower-case file name there.

rsahelpers 0.1.0

  • The package has been renamed from splinecongruence to rsahelpers to support a broader collection of response surface analysis utilities.

  • classify_yao_ma() classifies Mplus or parameter-table response surfaces using significance-based rules or user-supplied practical-equivalence margins, with diagnostic partial and indeterminate results.

  • create_rsa_mplus_model() and the related write, run, read, and workflow helpers now generate full latent and reliability-corrected SI-LMS response surface models, including XWITH interactions, surface constraints, and an explicit USEVARIABLES statement.

  • predictor_coverage() and plot_predictor_coverage() summarize and display sparse regions in the joint distribution of commensurate X/Y scale scores.

  • read_rsa_mplus_model() can attach a cached or relocated Mplus output to an existing workflow while preserving its role metadata.

  • RSA_mplus() is now the canonical implementation for extracting polynomial coefficients from Mplus output and optionally plotting them with RSA; it now also accepts fitted workflow and mplusObject inputs and infers generated model labels automatically. Three-dimensional plots annotate a1 through a5 with APA-style significance stars when Mplus constraint p-values are available. With ESTIMATOR = BAYES, the 95% credibility interval is used for the significance decision instead of the one-tailed posterior p-value, so a single * marks surface parameters whose interval excludes zero. The interval bounds are also returned in new_parameters as lower_2.5ci and upper_2.5ci.

  • rsahelpers no longer declares or installs franzpak. The two packages previously listed each other in Suggests and Remotes, which made their dependency resolution circular and coupled their CI. The dependency is now one-directional: franzpak’s deprecated RSA_mplus() forwards here, and the optional franzpak coefficient table in the Mplus vignette is guarded by requireNamespace().

Centering, scaling, and seams

  • fit_piecewise_congruence(), fit_spline_congruence(), and prepare_congruence_data() now use the consistent formula interface Z ~ X * Y instead of separate wanted, actual, and outcome arguments.
  • Pooled centering and scaling are now the default (center = "pooled", scale = "pooled"), following the RSA package, so the X = Y congruence interpretation is preserved out of the box. center/scale accept "pooled", "variablewise", and "none"; logical center is still accepted for backward compatibility (TRUE = variablewise, FALSE = none, with no scaling unless scale is given explicitly).
  • prepare_congruence_data(), fit_spline_congruence(), and fit_piecewise_congruence() gain a hinge_offset argument that parameterizes the previously hardcoded Y = X ± 1 fixed two-seam hinges. The offset is in working-scale units (i.e. SD units under pooled scaling).
  • fit_spline_congruence() gains a fix argument to hold parameters constant (e.g. fix = c(c0 = 0, c1 = 1)) for a constrained nested fit.

Inference and model comparison

  • bootstrap_spline() now routes through boot::boot.ci() and supports type = "perc", "basic", "norm", and "bca". The bootstrap failure rate is reported via a warning and a fail_rate attribute.
  • New compare_spline_models() and anova() method build nested-model comparison tables (ΔR², F on ΔRSS, df, p, AIC) with a guard that flags when a larger model fits worse than the simpler model nested within it.
  • select_spline_congruence() selects a linear, fixed-LOC, or free one-seam surface using residual-bootstrap likelihood-ratio tests and arm-coverage diagnostics; absolute-difference, piecewise, and two-seam fits are retained as benchmarks or sensitivity analyses.
  • New logLik(), nobs(), and summary() methods for congruence_spline, enabling AIC()/BIC() and a coefficient table with delta-method standard errors, t statistics, and p-values.
  • spline_tests() omits invalid Wald tests of seam existence and seam count; its remaining seam-location and shape tests are conditional on a supported one-seam surface. summary() and spline_tests() warn (controllable via warn_seam) that delta-method standard errors for seam parameters are approximate because the Jacobian is evaluated at the non-differentiable seam; the bootstrap is recommended for seam inference.
  • spline_surface_features() now reports two-seam section slopes and a seam-crossing diagnostic (seams_cross, crossing_x, n_sections).
  • tidy_piecewise_summary() now includes std.error, statistic, and p.value.

Plotting

  • plot_spline_surface() now shades facets by predicted outcome on a high-contrast diverging palette (RSA-style), uses larger tiles by default, and adds show_fit_line to optionally drop the theoretical X = Y line.
  • New plot_spline_contour() draws a 2D ggplot2 heatmap with contour lines and seam overlays (requires ggplot2).

Initial release notes

  • Initial package version with Edwards-Parry one- and two-seam spline regression helpers, OLS comparison models, Wald tests, bootstrap intervals, and base R surface plotting.
